_provenance.what: The Kālasetu Siddhānta long-span engine's fitted numbers: corrections on the Later Sūrya Siddhānta's own mean-motion count, the orbit of each body, and the measured amplitudes of the further terms.
_provenance.target: source/data/kalasetu-reference.json: JPL DE422 over about 3000 BCE – 3000 CE; beyond it, the Sun and planets from a numerical integration started from DE422's own states (source/tools/nbody.mjs), and the Moon and true node from astronomy-engine brought onto DE422's tidal acceleration. Apparent geocentric, true ecliptic of date, Samanvaya–Ecliptic frame; the mean node against the published polynomial.
_provenance.span: 5000 BCE – 3600 CE (astronomical years -4999 to 3600), 3,600 instants, hashed half held back. Every residual below is the held-back half's unless labelled fit. Bias is the mean signed residual (engine − reference).
_provenance.notTheText: Not the Sūrya Siddhānta's answer. The time-count is the text's; the geometry is not — see the header of kalasetu-engine.js for exactly what was added and from where.
_provenance.limits: Agreement with the reference above. Before 3000 BCE the planets rest on the integration (checked against DE422 across DE422's own 6000 years) and the Moon on a corrected extrapolation whose uncertainty grows as the square of the time; ΔT is uncertain by hours at 5000 BCE and by most of a day at 13000 BCE.
_provenance.units: residuals in arcminutes of longitude (latitude where given)

moon.note: fitted on DE422's instants; outside about 3000 BCE – 3000 CE the Moon is this fit's own extrapolation, and its residuals there are against astronomy-engine's corrected Moon, not an independent reference

integrator_check.note: heliocentric direction, arcseconds, integration minus DE422 after starting from DE422 at 3000 BCE

moon_correction.note: arcseconds; T in Julian centuries from J2000; residual rms is the scatter left on the overlap

modern_vs_reference.note: the modern engine (astronomy-engine) minus this reference, arcminutes, on the verification draw

Rāhu (true).against: the osculating node of DE422's Moon (beyond DE422: of astronomy-engine's, corrected)
